solutions.explanation:
The two radicals in the numerator have radicands whose product is \(5-4=1\). Squaring their sum will therefore simplify the nested radicals.

Let
\[
F=\frac{\sqrt{\sqrt5+2}+\sqrt{\sqrt5-2}}{\sqrt{\sqrt5+1}}.
\]
Since \(\sqrt5>2\), these radicands are positive, the denominator is nonzero, and \(F>0\). Expanding the numerator's square gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\left(\sqrt{\sqrt5+2}+\sqrt{\sqrt5-2}\right)^2
&=2\sqrt5+2\sqrt{(\sqrt5+2)(\sqrt5-2)}\\
&=2\sqrt5+2.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
F^2=\frac{2\sqrt5+2}{\sqrt5+1}=2.
\]
Because \(F\) is positive, this proves \(F=\sqrt2\).

For the remaining radical, recognize
\[
3-2\sqrt2=(\sqrt2-1)^2.
\]
The principal square root is nonnegative, and \(\sqrt2-1>0\), so
\[
\sqrt{3-2\sqrt2}=\sqrt2-1.
\]
Thus
\[
N=\sqrt2-(\sqrt2-1)=\boxed{1},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
solutions.title: Simplify by squaring and recognizing a perfect square
